units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 6. An internal service inquiry must be completed within no more than 60 calendar days from the decision to conduct it. Its duration may be extended to 90 calendar days by the persons who made that decision. Upon completion, the results shall be reported in a written conclusion to the employer's representative who ordered the inquiry.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 7. A civil servant subject to an internal service inquiry may be temporarily suspended from the civil service position held for the duration of the inquiry, with retention of the monetary remuneration for that position during that period. Such temporary suspension shall be effected by the employer's representative who ordered the inquiry.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 8. A civil servant subject to an internal service inquiry shall have the right to:
units.label: Part 8 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 1) give oral or written explanations and submit statements, requests and other documents;
units.label: Point 1 Part 8 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 2) appeal to the employer's representative who ordered the inquiry against decisions and actions (inaction) of the civil servants conducting it;
units.label: Point 2 Part 8 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 3) upon completion of the inquiry, examine the written conclusion and other materials relating to its results, unless this conflicts with requirements prohibiting disclosure of information constituting a state secret or another secret protected by federal law.
units.label: Point 3 Part 8 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 9. The written conclusion on the results of the internal service inquiry shall specify:
units.label: Part 9 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 1) the facts and circumstances established by the inquiry;
units.label: Point 1 Part 9 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 2) a proposal to impose or not to impose a disciplinary sanction on the civil servant.
units.label: Point 2 Part 9 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 10. The written conclusion on the results of the internal service inquiry shall be signed by the head of the state body's state service and personnel unit and other participants in the inquiry, and added to the personal file of the civil servant who was the subject of the inquiry.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Internal service inquiry
units.text: 11. Procedures for conducting internal service inquiries may be approved by regulatory legal acts of federal state bodies and public authorities of a federal territory for federal civil servants, and by regulatory legal acts of constituent entities of the Russian Federation for their civil servants, respectively, taking into account the provisions of this Article.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59.1. Sanctions for failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, and for failure to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption
units.text: Article 59.1. Sanctions for failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, and for failure to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption
units.label: Art. 59.1

units.locator: Article 59.1. Sanctions for failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, and for failure to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption
units.text: 1. The following sanctions shall be imposed for a civil servant's failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, or to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption by this Federal Law, Federal Law 273-ФЗ of 25 December 2008 ‘On Combating Corruption’ and other federal laws:
units.label: Part 1 Art. 59.1

units.locator: Article 59.1. Sanctions for failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, and for failure to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption
units.text: 1) an admonition;
units.label: Point 1 Part 1 Art. 59.1

units.locator: Article 59.1. Sanctions for failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, and for failure to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption
units.text: 2) a reprimand;
units.label: Point 2 Part 1 Art. 59.1

units.locator: Article 59.1. Sanctions for failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, and for failure to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption
units.text: 3) a warning of incomplete suitability for the position.
units.label: Point 3 Part 1 Art. 59.1

units.locator: Article 59.1. Sanctions for failure to comply with restrictions and prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, and for failure to perform duties established for the purpose of combating corruption
units.text: 2. A civil servant shall be exempt from liability for failure to comply with restrictions, prohibitions or requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, or to perform duties established by this Federal Law and other federal laws for the purpose of combating corruption, if that non-compliance or failure is recognized as resulting from circumstances beyond their control under the procedure provided for in parts 3–6 of Article 13 of Federal Law No. 273-ФЗ of 25 December 2008 ‘On Combating Corruption’.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 59.1

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.label: Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 1. A civil servant shall be dismissed due to loss of confidence in the event of:
units.label: Part 1 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 1) failure to take measures to prevent and (or) resolve a conflict of interest to which the civil servant is a party, except in cases established by federal laws;
units.label: Point 1 Part 1 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 2) failure to submit information on income, property and property-related obligations provided for by Federal Law No. 273-ФЗ of 25 December 2008 ‘On Combating Corruption’ and information on expenditure provided for by Federal Law No. 230-ФЗ of 3 December 2012 ‘On Monitoring the Correspondence between Expenditure of Persons Holding State Offices and Other Persons and Their Income’; submission of knowingly incomplete information, except in cases established by federal laws; or submission of knowingly inaccurate information;
units.label: Point 2 Part 1 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 3) participation for remuneration in the activities of the management body of a commercial organization, except in cases established by federal law;
units.label: Point 3 Part 1 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 4) engaging in entrepreneurial activities;
units.label: Point 4 Part 1 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 5) membership of management bodies, boards of trustees, supervisory boards or other bodies of foreign non-profit non-governmental organizations or their structural subdivisions operating in the Russian Federation, unless otherwise provided for by an international treaty of the Russian Federation or the legislation of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point 5 Part 1 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 6) breach by the civil servant, their spouse and minor children of the prohibition on opening or holding accounts (deposits), keeping cash or valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation, or owning and (or) using foreign financial instruments, except in cases established by federal laws.
units.label: Point 6 Part 1 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 2. An employer's representative who becomes aware that a civil servant has a personal interest that leads or may lead to a conflict of interest shall also be dismissed due to loss of confidence if the representative fails to take measures to prevent and (or) resolve a conflict of interest involving a subordinate civil servant, except in cases established by federal laws.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.2. Dismissal due to loss of confidence
units.text: 3. Information on imposition on a civil servant of the sanction of dismissal due to loss of confidence for a corruption offence shall be entered by the state body in which the civil servant served in the register of persons dismissed due to loss of confidence provided for in Article 15 of Federal Law No. 273-ФЗ of 25 December 2008 ‘On Combating Corruption’.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 59.2

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.label: Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 1. The sanctions provided for in Articles 59.1 and 59.2 of this Federal Law shall be imposed by the employer's representative on the basis of a report on an inspection conducted by the relevant state body's personnel service unit for prevention of corruption and other offences, or by an authorized unit of the Administration of the President of the Russian Federation in accordance with Article 13.4 of Federal Law No. 273-ФЗ of 25 December 2008 ‘On Combating Corruption’; if the inspection report was referred to the commission for resolving conflicts of interest, its recommendation shall also serve as a basis. With the civil servant's consent and provided that they admit committing a corruption offence, a sanction other than dismissal due to loss of confidence may be imposed on the basis of a report by the relevant state body's personnel service unit for prevention of corruption and other offences, setting out the factual circumstances of the corruption offence, and the civil servant's written explanation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 2. When imposing the sanctions provided for in Articles 59.1 and 59.2 of this Federal Law, account shall be taken of the nature and seriousness of the civil servant's corruption offence, the circumstances in which it was committed, compliance with other restrictions and prohibitions and requirements to prevent or resolve conflicts of interest, performance of duties established for the purpose of combating corruption, and previous results of the civil servant's performance of official duties.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 3. The sanctions provided for in Articles 59.1 and 59.2 of this Federal Law shall be imposed no later than six months after receipt of information that the civil servant committed a corruption offence, excluding periods of temporary incapacity for work, leave and other absence from service for valid reasons, and no later than three years after the offence was committed. Time spent on criminal proceedings shall not be included in those periods.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 3.1. An admonition may be imposed on a civil servant where their corruption offence is insignificant.
units.label: Part 3.1 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 4. An act imposing a sanction on a civil servant for a corruption offence shall cite Article 59.1 or 59.2 of this Federal Law as the ground for the sanction.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 5. A copy of the act imposing a sanction on a civil servant, specifying the corruption offence and the regulatory legal acts whose provisions were breached, or of the act declining to impose such a sanction, stating the reasons, shall be delivered to the civil servant against signature within five days after the relevant act is issued.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 6. A civil servant may appeal against a sanction in writing to the state body's service disputes commission or to a court.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Article 59.3. Procedure for imposing sanctions for corruption offences
units.text: 7. If, within one year from imposition of a sanction, a civil servant has not been subjected to a disciplinary sanction provided for in point 1, 2 or 3 of part 1 of Article 57 of this Federal Law, or a sanction provided for in point 1, 2 or 3 of Article 59.1 of this Federal Law, they shall be deemed to have no sanction.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 59.3

units.locator: Chapter 13. FORMATION OF THE CIVIL SERVICE PERSONNEL COMPLEMENT
units.text: Chapter 13. FORMATION OF THE CIVIL SERVICE PERSONNEL COMPLEMENT
units.label: Chapter 13. FORMATION OF THE CIVIL SERVICE PERSONNEL COMPLEMENT

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.label: Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 1. The civil service personnel complement of a state body shall be formed on the basis of the following principles:
units.label: Part 1 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 1) appointment of civil servants to civil service positions taking into account their merits in professional service activities;
units.label: Point 1 Part 1 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 2) improvement of civil servants' professional level.
units.label: Point 2 Part 1 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 2. Priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement shall be:
units.label: Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 1) training personnel for civil service and professional development of civil servants;
units.label: Point 1 Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 2) facilitating civil servants' career advancement on a competitive basis;
units.label: Point 2 Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 3) rotation of civil servants;
units.label: Point 3 Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 4) formation and effective use of the personnel reserve;
units.label: Point 4 Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 5) assessment of civil servants' professional service activity results through attestation;
units.label: Point 5 Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 6) use of modern personnel technologies upon entry into and during civil service.
units.label: Point 6 Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Principles and priority areas for forming the civil service personnel complement
units.text: 3. Repealed with effect from 1 January 2013. — Federal Law No. 395-ФЗ of 06.12.2011.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.label: Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 1. Civil servants shall be rotated to improve the effectiveness of civil service and combat corruption by appointing them to other civil service positions in the same or another state body.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 2. Federal civil servants shall be rotated in territorial bodies of federal executive bodies exercising control and supervisory functions. Federal civil servants holding the positions of heads of those bodies shall be subject to rotation. Rotation of federal civil servants holding other federal civil service positions in the ‘managers’ category whose duties involve control or supervisory functions in territorial bodies of a federal executive body whose activities are directed by the President of the Russian Federation or the Government of the Russian Federation may be conducted under a list of positions approved by the head of the federal executive body; in territorial bodies of a federal executive body subordinate to a federal ministry, it may be conducted under a list approved by the head of the federal executive body in agreement with the federal minister.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 2.1. Repealed. — Federal Law No. 461-ФЗ of 11.12.2018.
units.label: Part 2.1 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 2.2. Rotation of federal civil servants may be conducted:
units.label: Part 2.2 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 1) in federal executive bodies whose activities are directed by the President of the Russian Federation, under lists of federal civil service positions approved by the President of the Russian Federation and drawn up on the basis of proposals from those federal executive bodies;
units.label: Point 1 Part 2.2 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 2) in federal executive bodies whose activities are directed by the Government of the Russian Federation, under lists of federal civil service positions approved by the Government of the Russian Federation and drawn up on the basis of proposals from those federal executive bodies;
units.label: Point 2 Part 2.2 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 3) in other federal state bodies, under lists of federal civil service positions approved by the President of the Russian Federation and drawn up on the basis of proposals from the heads of those federal state bodies, under the procedure established by the President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Point 3 Part 2.2 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 3. The rotation plan for federal civil servants shall be approved by the head of the federal state body. The form of the rotation plan and the procedure for its approval shall be established by the federal executive body authorized by the Government of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 4. Rotation of a federal civil servant holding a federal civil service position in a federal executive body or its territorial body, or in another federal state body, to another federal executive body or its territorial body, or to another federal state body, shall be conducted by agreement between the heads of the relevant federal executive bodies and (or) other federal state bodies empowered to appoint to and release from the federal civil service position subject to rotation. Rotation of a federal civil servant to a federal executive body subordinate to a federal ministry, or to a territorial body of such a federal executive body, shall also require agreement with the federal minister.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 5. When a civil servant is appointed by rotation to another civil service position, their professional level, speciality, field of training and length of civil service or work in their speciality or field of training shall be taken into account. A civil servant shall be appointed by rotation to a civil service position whose position salary is no lower than that of the position they currently hold, except in the case provided for in this part. With their written consent, a civil servant may be appointed by rotation to a civil service position with a lower position salary than that of the position they hold. A civil servant may be appointed to a civil service position by rotation during the final year of a fixed-term service contract at the times provided for in the federal state body's rotation plan for federal state civil servants.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 6. A civil service position shall be held by rotation for a term of three to five years, unless otherwise provided for by this Federal Law.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 6.1. A civil servant's term in a civil service position held by rotation may be extended by decision of the employer's representative and with the civil servant's written consent. The employer's representative shall decide on extension, taking into account the recommendation of the commission for resolving conflicts of interest, no later than seven months before the civil servant's service contract expires.
units.label: Part 6.1 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 6.2. A civil servant may not hold the same civil service position to which they were appointed by rotation for more than ten years.
units.label: Part 6.2 Art. 60.1

units.locator: Article 60.1. Rotation of civil servants
units.text: 7. At least six months before the civil servant's service contract expires, the employer's representative shall notify the civil servant in writing, against signature, of their forthcoming appointment by rotation to another civil service position, specifying the terms of the service contract for the new position, or of the forthcoming extension of their term in the civil service position held by rotation, specifying the terms of the new service contract for that position.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 60.1
